subject: Clarify DPA routing: derivative rights, subprocessor controls, and transfer carveouts
messages:
From: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@atlascare.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@atlascare.com
Date: 2027-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: DPA questions re: derivative rights + subprocessor routing for POC

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for yesterday's call — appreciate the quick turnaround on the POC timeline. Before we proceed to procurement, our legal team asked for one more clarification on the DPA: specifically, whether Redwood will commit to a carveout that prevents model improvement from using AtlasCare PII (i.e., a no-training/no-aggregate-learning clause), and how derivative output ownership is scoped in multi-tenant hosted mode.

We also need to confirm the subprocessor routing rules for cross-border routing: if a subprocessor is changed during the term, do customers get notified and do they get an option to keep traffic routed only to onshore processing? AtlasCare requires an onshore-only option for Protected Health Information for our pilot.

I've attached our standard vendor questionnaire and a redline of the DPA we typically send vendors. Can Redwood indicate: 1) what language you can accept for no-training guarantees (and any operational evidence you can provide), and 2) whether you can support per-account routing constraints tied to contractual obligations?

Looking forward — we need responses by EOD Friday to keep the procurement window.

Best,
Lena
Security & Privacy Operations
AtlasCare

Attachments: AtlasCare_Vendor_Questionnaire.docx (docx), AtlasCare_DPA_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@atlascare.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions re: derivative rights + subprocessor routing for POC

Hi Lena — thanks, and great questions. Looping in David (legal) and Marissa (privacy) so we can be explicit. High level answers below; see the attached redline (Redwood_DPA_response_v1.pdf) and a proposed operational checklist.

1) No-training / model improvement: Redwood can commit that AtlasCare customer data for the POC will not be used to further train or improve any general-purpose model. We propose a DPA clause that: 1) explicitly prohibits using customer inputs or derived outputs for model training; 2) records the commitment in our control plane per tenant; and 3) provides an audit report on training-output flags on request. Operational evidence we can provide: audit log extract showing "learning_enabled=false" for the account, exportable request/response sample scrubbed for PHI, and an ops runbook describing our learning toggle.

2) Output / derivative ownership: Redwood's standard approach is to grant customers an output license to responses generated from their inputs. We can add contract language clarifying that AtlasCare retains exclusive rights to Customer Inputs and to any unredacted Customer-derived outputs for the POC; Redwood retains rights to general model improvements derived from publicly available or synthetic training only. We will not assert ownership over customer prompts/responses.

3) Subprocessor routing & onshore-only option: We support region-based routing policies. For the POC we can define an onshore-only subrouting profile that pins requests to US-only subprocessors and infrastructure. If subprocessors change during the term, we provide 30 days' notice and will implement a migration path; for PHI use-cases we can include a contractual right to reject a new subprocessor that would cause offshoring. There are operational constraints (e.g., capacity, latency); we'll note those in the service appendix.

I'll let David add the legal redline notes and Marissa add the evidence checklist items. If AtlasCare wants a stronger contractual onshore-residency guarantee, we can propose a Dedicated (reserved) deployment as an alternative.

Actionable next steps: I'll push the redline and a short evidence pack by EOD tomorrow. If that timing doesn't work for your procurement window, please tell us and we'll prioritize.

Thanks — Priyom
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_response_v1.pdf (pdf), operational_evidence_checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@atlascare.com>, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-02T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions re: derivative rights + subprocessor routing for POC

Lena — quick legal clarifications inline.

On Dec 1, 2027, at 11:03 AM, Priyom Das wrote:
> 1) No-training / model improvement: Redwood can commit that AtlasCare customer data for the POC will not be used to further train or improve any general-purpose model.

We will propose the following contract language in the DPA redline (short form):
"Redwood shall not use Customer Data for model training, fine-tuning, or to augment any models intended for general-purpose or third-party use. Redwood may process Customer Data for purposes of delivering the Services, debugging, and short-term caching, provided such processing is not used to derive model parameter updates. Any deviation requires Customer's prior written consent."

Operational proof: a monthly audit extract and the account-level toggle export are acceptable forms of evidence. For AtlasCare's PHI needs we recommend adding a companion Statement of Work that identifies data classes and the onshore routing requirement.

On outputs: Priyom's suggested output-rights language looks good, but we will add an explicit carveout that forbids Redwood from asserting exclusive rights over Customer-specific prompts and generated outputs, including for derivative works arising solely from Customer Data.

On subprocessors: We can agree to 30-days' notice and a right to object for onshore-only accounts. Note: objection rights should be reasonable (e.g., based on whether the proposed subprocessor would cause relevant data to be processed outside permitted territories). We will include an SLA addendum that explains capacity fallback if the onshore routing profile is congested.

Please confirm whether the AtlasCare team will accept the redlined DPA plus the operational evidence pack as final for procurement, or whether you need a Dedicated deployment quote. If you accept the DPA redline, we can provide a proforma amendment to lock in the onshore routing profile.

Thanks,
David
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@atlascare.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@atlascare.com
Date: 2027-12-03T08:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions re: derivative rights + subprocessor routing for POC

David/Priyom — thanks for the quick & detailed responses. Procurement is OK with the redline as long as evidence and the onshore routing opt are included in the SOW. Two clarifying asks before we circulate internally: 1) confirm the exact evidence artifacts (e.g., example audit export columns, frequency of reports), and 2) confirm whether the "right to object" to a new subprocessor is a veto for onshore-only accounts or a request to negotiate (procurement wants veto-like assurance for PHI in the pilot).

Procurement also asked about remedial remedies if Redwood were to inadvertently process PHI offshore during the POC (e.g., notification SLA, corrective migration, potential credits). Would you propose language for that?

If we can get the evidence checklist and a short clause on remediation by EOD Friday, procurement can proceed to the PO stage next week.

Regards,
Lena

Attachments included earlier remain relevant.

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@atlascare.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-05T16:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions re: derivative rights + subprocessor routing for POC

Lena — attaching the evidence checklist and a remediation clause draft; below are the key artifacts and the remediation steps we propose.

Key evidence artifacts (we'll share as exportable CSVs):
- Account-level learning flag export (field: account_id, learning_enabled=false, timestamp, operator_id) -- monthly and on-demand
- Audit log extract (fields: request_id, timestamp, source_ip, region, processing_node_id, subprocessor_id) -- rolling 90 days, snapshot on request
- Sample anonymized request/response bundle (PHI redacted) for ops verification -- available on request with NDA

Proposed remediation clause (short form):
"In the event Redwood identifies or is notified that Customer Data subject to the onshore-only routing profile was processed outside the permitted territory, Redwood will: (a) notify Customer within 24 hours; (b) suspend the implicated processing pipeline within 48 hours and migrate processing to an onshore-compliant environment; (c) provide a root-cause analysis and evidence of remediation within 10 business days; and (d) offer a service credit calculated as 10% of the monthly invoice for the impacted service week, unless the parties agree an alternative remedy."

Regarding the objection right: for onshore-only PHI accounts we will include a contractual veto right for new subprocessors that would result in offshoring of covered data; veto must be exercised within 30 days of notice. If the veto is exercised and Redwood cannot provide an equivalent onshore alternative within 30 days, Redwood will propose a commercial workaround (e.g., Dedicated capacity or temporary suspension) and will consult with AtlasCare procurement/legal on next steps.

I'll upload the redline DPA with these edits and the evidence checklist to the Drive folder and a DocuSign envelope for signature. If that looks good I can get procurement a PO-ready statement of work that pins the onshore routing profile for the pilot.

If you want, we can schedule a 20-min call tomorrow to walk procurement through the evidence artifacts.

Thanks,
Priyom
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
